verses.1: And Elyahu said, “Stand among the people of Gilad and go to Ahava. May the LORD, the God of Israel, be with you. I have stood before him. Whether these years will be years of rain and abundance, or not, it depends on my words.”
verses.2: And the word of Jehovah was to him:
verses.3: Go from here, and turn towards the east. You will be hidden in a ravine that lies at the foot of the mountain.
verses.4: And from that stream, you shall drink. And I commanded the evening clouds to nourish you there.
verses.5: And he went and did what the LORD commanded him. He sat down by the river Krit, which is located in front of the Jordan River.
verses.6: And in the morning, they bring him bread and meat. In the evening, they still bring him bread and meat. And from the stream, water flows down.
verses.7: And after some time passed, the stream dried up, because there was no rain on the land.
verses.9: Stand up, you woman who is beside him. You shall sit there. Now, I command that a woman without any ability to speak be given to you.
verses.10: And he stood up, went to Zarpatha, and came to the gates of the city. There he saw a woman who was skilled in making wooden instruments. He called out to her and said, “Please give me some water to drink, and I will build a fire for myself.”
verses.11: And she went to get it. She called out to her, saying, “Please give me some bread to eat with your hands.”
verses.12: And He said, “Holy God, your servant has no other choice but to do this: I will gather some wood from the forest, and I will also gather some vinegar from the jar. Then I will make fire with these two pieces of wood, and I will use them for me and my son. After that, we will eat them together.”
verses.13: And he said to her, “Eliyahu, do not be afraid. Do as you are told. But first, make a small hole in it. Then take it out for me. And you can use it to plant something later.”
verses.14: For as Jehovah, the God of Israel, has said: “When the wine is ready, it will not run out; and when the honey is ready, it will not be lost. Until the day when Jehovah brings rain upon the earth.”
verses.15: And she went and did what Elijah commanded her. She ate both him and his food. And in her house, days passed.
verses.16: When the pot was filled, it didn’t overflow; and the wine in it wasn’t lost, as the Lord had commanded through Elijah.
verses.17: After these events, the daughter of the woman fell ill in the house. Her illness became extremely severe, to the point that no one could cure her.
verses.18: And he said to Elijah, “What do I have to do? You are a man of God. You have come to me to tell me that my son will die, and to bring this news to me.”
verses.19: And he said to her, “Give me your son.” She took him from her arms and brought him to the upper room where she would sit. Then she laid him on her lap.
verses.20: And he called out to the LORD, and said, “Lord, my God, have mercy on this woman who I am carrying with me. Let her die so that her child may not be born.”
verses.21: And he anointed the child three times. Then he called out to Jehovah and said, “Yahweh, your servant, please let the soul of this child rest upon its own body.”
verses.22: And Jehovah heard the cry of Elijah. The child’s spirit returned to him, and he lived again.
verses.23: And Elijah took the child and carried him down from the upper room. Then he gave the child to his mother. Elijah said, “Look, this is your son.”
verses.24: And the woman said to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God, and that the words of Jehovah are true in your mouth.”
